cards.b: Identify, satisfy and anticipate customer needs; maintain customer loyalty; build customer relationships; gain information about customers.

cards.f: Why markets have become more competitive
cards.b: Globalisation (foreign firms enter), online selling (easy price comparison), better transport.
Mass: same product to the whole market. Niche: a small, specific part of the market; less competition and higher prices.
An identifiable sub-group of a market whose consumers have similar characteristics or preferences.
Income/socio-economic group, age, gender, location, lifestyle or use of the product.
Market-orientated: research what consumers want, then make it. Product-orientated: make what it can, then try to sell it.
Gathering, analysing and interpreting information about a market.
Original, first-hand data collected for the business's own purpose (questionnaire, interview, focus group, observation, test marketing).
Using information already collected by someone else (sales records, government statistics, internet). Cheaper but may be out of date.
Up to date, specific to needs and not available to competitors; but expensive and time-consuming.
A small group led by a researcher who discuss a product. Gives detailed opinions but is costly and members influence each other.
A group of people selected to respond to a survey because asking the whole population is too costly and slow.
Random: every member of the population has an equal chance. Quota: set numbers chosen by characteristics such as age and gender.

cards.f: Why market research may be inaccurate
cards.b: Small or unrepresentative sample, leading questions, bias, out-of-date data. Shows what people say, not always what they do.
(New − original) ÷ original × 100. Always divide by the ORIGINAL value.

short.q: Distinguish between a niche market and a mass market. [2]
short.model: A niche market is a small specialised segment of a larger market. A mass market has very large sales with no targeting of particular groups.

short.q: Explain two advantages of secondary research. [4]
short.model: It is cheaper and quicker because the data already exists. It also gives overall market data such as size and trends.

short.q: Explain why the results of a questionnaire might be inaccurate. [3]
short.model: The sample may be too small or unrepresentative. Leading questions can bias answers, and people may say what they will do but not actually do it.

short.q: Calculate the percentage increase in market sales from $2.5 million to $3.0 million. [2]
Explain two benefits to a business of segmenting its market. [4]
short.model: It can match products and promotion to each segment's needs, raising sales. It also avoids wasted advertising and can reveal gaps in the market.
